text: This lab combines everything from the chapter into one working feature: stopping a Change Request from being plannable inside an active change freeze window, like a blackout period around quarter-end or a major release.

Three pieces work together. A Script Include method, isDateInFreezeWindow, answers true or false for a given date. An onChange script on planned_start_date warns the user immediately after they pick a date. And an onSubmit script does the real enforcement, using the async-safe pattern from the previous lesson.

The onChange script calls the Script Include through GlideAjax and shows an error message if the date lands inside a freeze window - but notice it can't actually block anything. By the time its callback runs with the real answer, the onChange function itself has already finished. It's purely advisory; enforcement is onSubmit's job.

onSubmit needs to run twice: once to kick off the check, and once more after it passes. A plain local variable wouldn't survive between those two separate calls, so a hidden backing field, u underscore freeze check passed, carries that result instead. The guard at the top checks that field first; if it's not yet true, the script fires the GlideAjax call and returns false, blocking only this attempt.

Inside the callback, if the date is frozen, an error message appears and the form stays open. If it's clear, the callback sets the hidden field to true and calls g_form.submit() itself - which re-runs onSubmit from the top. This time the guard sees the flag already set and returns true immediately, and the record actually saves.

That's the whole chapter in one feature: g_form reading and writing the form, the three script types with onSubmit's special return-value behavior, and the block-first, submit-in-the-callback pattern for anything that needs an async server check. Next up, Chapter Six: the Script Debugger, for stepping through server-side JavaScript line by line when something doesn't behave the way you expect.
